title: Check yourself: instance and static members

questions.stem: Plugin declares `static final List<String> LOADED = new ArrayList<>();`. AuditPlugin extends Plugin and has `static { LOADED.add("audit"); }`. Nothing else has touched either class when the application runs `System.out.println(AuditPlugin.LOADED);`. What does it print?

options.text: [audit], since the expression names AuditPlugin, so AuditPlugin is set up before the field is read
options.says: naming a class is not an active use of it; the field read is a use of the class that declares the field

options.text: [audit], since the JVM sets up every class on the class path when it loads the application
options.says: a class is initialized on its first active use, not at startup

options.text: [], since the field is declared in Plugin, so reading it sets up Plugin and not its subclass
options.says: reading a static field initializes the class that declares it; AuditPlugin's static block never runs

options.text: [], since a class's static blocks are run when the first object of that class is made
options.says: a call to a static method, Class.forName or a subclass's initialization also initializes a class; here nothing uses AuditPlugin at all

origin.section: A Class Is Initialized on Its First Active Use, Not When Its Name Appears

questions.stem: A library has `public static final int PAGE_SIZE = 50;` and `public static int maxPages() { return 40; }`. The reporting app, compiled against it, prints `Paging.PAGE_SIZE + " and " + Paging.maxPages()`. The library changes the values to 20 and 10, and only the library jar is replaced. What does the app print now?

options.text: 50 and 10, since the field's value was copied into the app at build time and the method runs from the new jar
options.says: PAGE_SIZE is a constant variable, so javac copied 50 into the app; the method call is made at run time

options.text: 50 and 40, since the field's value and the method's result were both copied into the app at build time
options.says: only constant variables are copied into the reader; a method runs from the jar that is there at run time

options.text: 20 and 10, since the field is read from the new jar and the method runs from the new jar as well
options.says: a constant variable is not looked up at run time; its value was copied into the app

options.text: 20 and 40, since the field is read from the new jar and the method's result was copied into the app at build time
options.says: it is the other way round: the constant was copied in, the method is called

origin.section: A Constant Variable Is Compiled Into the Code That Reads It

questions.stem: `class Currencies { static final Currencies INSTANCE = new Currencies(); private static final Set<String> SUPPORTED = Set.of("EUR", "USD"); private final int count; Currencies() { count = SUPPORTED.size(); } }`. What happens the first time code reads `Currencies.INSTANCE`?

options.text: ExceptionInInitializerError, since the constructor runs while SUPPORTED still holds its default value
options.says: static initializers run top to bottom, so the constructor sees SUPPORTED's default, null, and size() throws

options.text: ExceptionInInitializerError, since the constructor runs while Currencies is still being initialized, which the JVM rejects
options.says: the JVM lets a static initializer create an instance of its own class; the trouble is the order of the fields

options.text: An instance with count 2, since SUPPORTED receives its value before any constructor of Currencies runs
options.says: static fields get their values in source order, and a constructor called in between sees the later ones' defaults

options.text: An instance with count 2, since javac copies the value of SUPPORTED into the constructor when it compiles
options.says: only a final primitive or String with a constant initializer is a constant variable; a Set is read at run time

origin.section: Static Initializers Run in Source Order, So an Early One Reads a Later Field's Default

questions.stem: GeoIp reads its database file in a static initializer. On one pod the file was missing when the first request used GeoIp, and that request failed. A minute later the file is copied into place. What do the requests that use GeoIp get from then on?

options.text: NoClassDefFoundError, since the JVM keeps GeoIp marked as failed and does not run its initializer again
options.says: a class whose initializer threw is marked failed and its initializer never runs again; every later use gets NoClassDefFoundError until the JVM restarts

options.text: NoClassDefFoundError, since the class loader discards GeoIp after the failure and cannot define it again
options.says: the class is still loaded; the error means its initialization failed, and the JVM remembers that

options.text: Correct answers, since the next use of GeoIp runs its static initializer again and now finds the file
options.says: a failed initializer is never run again in that JVM

options.text: Correct answers, since the first request's failure was handled and GeoIp then finished initializing
options.says: the failure belongs to the class, not the request: the class is marked failed and every later use fails until the JVM restarts

origin.section: A Static Initializer That Throws Leaves the Class Unusable Until the JVM Restarts
